episode_title: How to start an ABA Business?

real_qa.q: What are the main barriers holding people back from starting an ABA business?
real_qa.r: Common barriers include self-doubt about being good enough, worrying about lacking sufficient experience or capability, and fearing that someone else will do a better job. However, many of these are not real fears but ways of avoiding uncomfortable experiences. The key distinction is determining which concerns are legitimate and which are simply avoidance mechanisms rooted in human behavior.

real_qa.q: Why does April not recommend franchises or investors for starting an ABA business?
real_qa.r: April recommends building what you want to build rather than relying on franchises or investor models. She emphasizes that your business should reflect your own vision and values, not someone else's model. This allows you to make it your own, put your own spin on it, and bring what excites you into the company from the very beginning.
real_qa.requete: ABA business franchise vs building own

real_qa.q: How much startup capital did April and Steven have when they decided to start their ABA practice?
real_qa.r: When they decided to launch, they had one hundred thousand dollars in the bank set as their target savings threshold. They planned that Steven would put in his notice for his full-time job once they reached this amount. However, they acknowledged this amount ended up not being sufficient despite seeming like a large sum at the time they started in 2011.

real_qa.q: What does Vision as a survival tool mean for ABA business owners according to April?
real_qa.r: April states that 'Vision isn't a marketing tool. It's a survival tool.' She emphasizes you need to truly know what your vision is for the company because when times get hard—which they will—you need that personal attachment to your vision to keep going. Without a genuine vision that is yours, not someone else's, you will abandon the company when difficulties arise.

real_qa.q: How long did April and Steven operate their ABA practice before Steven left his full-time job?
real_qa.r: They started their ABA business in 2011 and Steven quit his full-time job in 2014, meaning the practice had been running for approximately three years before he transitioned to work on it full-time. One week after Steven put in his notice, they discovered April was pregnant.

guest.bio_context: April co-hosts the ABA Business Leaders podcast alongside Steven and shares her personal journey of starting an ABA practice. She describes her approach as being supportive and visionary, focusing on helping aspiring ABA entrepreneurs build their dream companies rather than following conventional templates. She emphasizes the importance of knowing one's 'why' and building intentionally rather than adopting franchise or investor models.
